Earned on every kill, spent at the Echo Altar; +10s rise where the kill falls.
The only gamble: a donated weapon with limited uses; the mask makes it fly to another city.
One model per class weapon; each tier makes its look and ability visibly stronger.
Mead, ales and draughts bought at the altar, shown as a row of icons.
Soulcaller's Staff, Wyrmspine Javelin, Mutagen Staff, Dragon Slayer: each earned by a hidden quest.
Felldir the Old whispers the steps; his story opens as cities are freed.
Each city's priest; the three word-dragons and the Echo of Alduin.
In a party a fallen player can be lifted; alone, the night ends.
Short drops from the dead - to be designed.
rules: Every weapon, ability and enemy is clear by its shape, colour and sound before you think about it - BO3's clarity.
Everything is built from Skyrim's own meshes, textures and sounds (and the DLCs'): nothing flat, nothing that looks 2D or pasted on.
Fire, frost, shock, shadowfire, holy, poison, arcane and blood each have one kit - colour, textures, sounds - used by every weapon, spell and flask of that element. No purple bolt that burns red.
A hit confirms with a sound and a short burst; no hit pause, no screen shake, no banners.
Every tier is visibly stronger than the last on the same model; Legendary adds a signature you can spot across the field.
Only what a BO3 player looks for: the night, the essence, the brews, the compass. Everything else appears when it matters.
Every effect is budgeted for a crowd of 30 or more; nothing that stutters the first time it plays.
Fewer mod requirements over time: our own models from Skyrim's meshes, our own effects from Skyrim's parts.
flow: A change you ask for, or one I propose and you approve, written as a feature in its system.
I build it; previews go in the workshop where they help you decide.
Each new effect is played in the Test Range on dummies; you record it with NVIDIA, and the clip comes into the workshop.
Installed on your PC; it appears in Now under its category with how to test it and what you should see.
You mark it (or pass a whole category at once). A fail goes straight back to Building with your note.
Passed and unchanged since; it stays in its system so it never comes back as a suggestion.

tabnew2.light: Throw it: it bursts into webs that stick the dead in place for 6 s while spiderlings bite them.

tabnew2.base: A spear with a mammoth's tusk for a head, bound in hide
tabnew2.heavy: A stampede of ghostly mammoths tramples the street ahead.

tabnew2.base: A hagraven's feathered fetish of bones and twine
tabnew2.light: Throw it: it curses 3 of the dead - they turn and fight for you for 10 s.

rolls.name: The Reel
rolls.about: The design we have now, remade: the glyph ring grinds round, ghostly weapons flicker in the centre like a reel slowing down, and the won one rises out of the face in its rarity's light.

rolls.about: BO3's box beam: a column of the rarity's light shoots into the sky from the Tablet; the weapons flick up inside it, faster then slower, and the won one hangs in the beam.

rolls.name: The Wheel
rolls.about: The weapons circle the Tablet on a ring of runes, spinning fast and easing to a stop with the won one in front; it floats in to you.

rolls.name: Soul Storm
rolls.about: A vortex of souls rises off the Tablet with the weapons tumbling in it; the storm collapses into the won one with a burst of its rarity's colour.

lore.title: The Curse
lore.lead: At Helgen, Alduin shouted SLEN TIID VO - his raising shout - into the earth, and every grave in Skyrim heard it. His voice now hangs like a mist over the road to Sovngarde: the dead cannot pass, and every night it throws them back down to Skyrim as red beams of light. The Echo Altars the old Tongues raised in every city went dark; wake them, city by city, and the dead sleep again. The questline ends right before Skyrim's own fight with Alduin.

a: Helgen burned. The World-Eater flew north over the smoke... and as he flew, he shouted into the earth.
Three words. SLEN... TIID... VO. Flesh. Time. Undo. The shout he raises his dragons with.
But this time it fell on every grave in Skyrim. And every grave heard it.

qa.q: Why do the dead come back?
a: His shout hangs like a mist over every road the dead walk. Shor's hall, Arkay's mercy, whatever waits for them... none of them can pass it.
They try, every night. The mist turns them back... and his voice throws them down to Skyrim again, as red light out of the sky.

qa.q: What are the red beams in the sky?
a: The dead, falling. Turned back from Sovngarde, and thrown down wherever his voice is strongest.
The red lightning is worse. That is how the strong ones come... the ones his voice holds tightest.
Echo Altars. The old Tongues raised one in every hold, long before your Empire, to answer a dragon's voice with their own.
When the World-Eater shouted, they went dark. Wake one, and its city's dead will sleep again.

qa.q: How do I wake an altar?
a: ...four trials... at night... the dead... the stone will show you...
...one city at a time... and then I will be clearer...
You have a dragon's soul in a mortal's body. When you kill one of the dead, the stone hears it the way it hears a shout.
The Tongues would have given anything to be what you are. Do not waste it.
What is left of his shout in the dead. When they fall, it comes out of them... and it comes to you.
The stone can make it into steel, and spells, and brews. Spend it. It does no good in your pocket.
The dead will drag you down. If anyone stands with you, they can lift you again. If no one does... the night ends without you.
Do not let it. I have lost enough people to the dark.

qa.q: What is the Tablet of Mysteries?
a: An old thing, and a strange one. The Tongues left weapons with it that they did not want to keep.
Feed it the essence, and it will give you one. It does not tell you which. Neither will I.

qa.q: Why do the cities teach me shouts?
a: Every freed city remembers a little of the Voice. They teach it to the one who freed them.
Use them. A shout is a weapon the dead cannot answer.
Two stones awake, and their voices carry to each other. That is how you hear me now.
Every stone you wake makes the mist thinner. Not gone... but thinner.

qa.q: Why one city at a time?
a: Each altar answers for its own hold. The dead of Whiterun do not care that Riverwood sleeps.
And each city has its keeper. A priest who swore an oath to the World-Eater... and remembers it.
Men who served the dragons when the dragons ruled. They wore masks of the dragons' faces, and took the dragons' power.
When the shout came, every one of them woke with his oath still in his mouth. They keep the altars dark for their master.
Break a city's seals, and its priest must come out to face you.
Four stones. Five. The mist trembles when the sixth wakes... I can feel it already.
At six... I will be able to tell you who I am. And something old will begin to stir.
The wonders. Four weapons, one for each path, hidden when the Tongues still walked. They sleep no longer.
Each waits for the one who walks its path. But none of them will simply be found. Each must be earned.
When yours is won, the Greybeards will call you to the mountain. The wonder waits beneath their hall.

qa.q: What do the Greybeards have to do with this?
a: High Hrothgar sits on the Throat of the World. Where the Tongues cast the World-Eater out of time.
Beneath it is a room the Greybeards guard and do not speak of. The wonders are kept there, until they are won.

qa.q: What is the echo on the summit?
a: When we cast him out of time, his voice did not all go with him. Part of it stayed behind, caught on the summit where we broke him.
It has circled there since, waiting. Now that he is back in the world, it answers him... and it is louder than ever.
He flies where he likes. The echo cannot leave the mountain. That is why you can reach it... and why breaking it breaks his hold on the dead.

qa.q: Every altar is awake. Is it over?
a: Every stone sings again. Listen... all of Skyrim answering at once. I have not heard that in a very long time.
But the World-Eater's voice is not gone. It lingers in the wild places... and in the echo he left on the summit.
The cities are safe. The rest of Skyrim is not. Not yet.

qa.q: The wonders are won. What now?
a: Now the words wake. Each of the three words of his shout was carried by a dragon. They are flying again.
SLEN in the Reach. TIID under Labyrinthian. VO on the peak of Mount Anthor. Silence all three.
Each will come at night, with a siege of the dead before it. And each one gives back what it stole.
Slenvahrin. The Flesh-Wyrm. It circles the cult's old shrine in the Reach, and the barrow-dead around it grow new flesh.
Kill it, and the strength the World-Eater poured into the dead will run in you instead.
Tiidrah. The Time-Wyrm. It sleeps under Labyrinthian, where the cult laid its dead by the thousand.
It gives the dead back the years the grave took. Take them from it... and the time is yours.
Vonahlok. The Undoing. It keeps the last word, on the frozen peak of Mount Anthor.
Where it flies, death itself comes undone. It is the oldest of the three... and the angriest.
I felt it fall. SLEN is silent... the dead in the Reach are only bones again. You are stronger for it.
TIID is silent. The time the dead stole is yours now. Spend it better than they did.
The Undoing has undone its last. I never thought I would hear VO go quiet.
Only their maker. On the summit of the Throat of the World, where we cast him out of time, his echo still circles.
It is not the World-Eater himself. Only the shape his voice left in the sky. It is enough to kill you.
Break it... and the curse breaks with it. Every grave in Skyrim will be quiet.

qa.q: How do I beat the Echo?
a: Bring everything you have earned. The wonder. The words you took from the three. And anyone who will stand with you.
It will call the dead of all Skyrim to the summit. Do not let them pull you away from it.
Here, it is. The echo is broken, and Skyrim's dead are sleeping again. The nights are only nights.
But the World-Eater himself still lives. Without his echo, he has nowhere left to hide... but Sovngarde.
He will go there to feed on the souls of the dead. That is where the last fight waits for you.

qa.q: What is the Hall of the Awakened?
a: A room beneath High Hrothgar that opened when the echo broke. The Tongues built it for whoever ended this.
It is yours now. Go and see it.

lore.title: Felldir the Old
lore.lead: The voice in the altar's centre stone - one of the three ancient Tongues who cast Alduin out of time. He speaks only from a freed altar, and his story opens as more cities are freed (his name is kept secret until six altars are free).

a: ...someone who has waited... too long... wake another stone...
Someone who was here when these stones were raised. That is all I can give you... for now.
My name is in the mist with everything else. Wake more stones, and it will come back to me.
Far. Behind the mist he left across the road to Sovngarde. I speak through the stones because I cannot speak any other way.
Older than your Empire. Older than the first Nord kings. They were raised while dragons still ruled the sky.
We raised them in secret, in the dark, where the dragons' priests would not see.
The three of us. The first who learned the Voice... and turned it on our masters.
One fell at the summit, before the end. One I have not seen since. And I... I am still here.
A warrior with a golden hilt. She was the bravest of us. She went at him first, and he took her first.
I watched her fall. I did not stop. That is what she would have wanted.
A warrior with one eye, who saw more than most with two. After the summit... I lost him in the mist.
Perhaps he is in Sovngarde, waiting for the road to open. I hope so.
Six stones are free... and I remember. I am Felldir. Felldir the Old.
It has been a very long time since anyone asked me that.

qa.q: What did you do at the summit?
a: I read the Elder Scroll. The others held him in the sky, and I read it... and the World-Eater was cast out of time.
We thought it was the end. We were young. We did not know that time has a way of giving things back.
I lived a long life after the summit, and died old, and took the road to Sovngarde. When he shouted at Helgen, the mist fell over it... with me still on it.
I cannot go forward, and I will not go back. So I wait... and I speak through the stones we raised.

qa.q: Have you been alone all this time?
a: The dead pass me in the mist. They cannot see the way. Neither can I. We are all lost together.
Then you came. The first living voice I have heard in a very long time.
Proud. Patient. He did not hate us. You do not hate the grass you walk on.
That is what frightened me most. Not his anger... his certainty.

qa.q: Did you know there would be a Dragonborn?
a: We hoped. The Scroll told us he would come back. It did not tell us who would be waiting when he did.
I am glad it was you.

qa.q: Who are the Greybeards to you?
a: They came after us. They took the Voice and made it quiet, and climbed the mountain to keep it safe.
We used it to fight. They use it to listen. Perhaps they are wiser than we were.
I did. For a long time. Then I was dead for longer than I was ever alive, and hate is hard to carry that far.
Now I only want them to stop. That is not the same thing.
To go home. Nothing more. They are not cruel... they are lost, and the World-Eater's voice is all they can hear.
When you put them down, you are not killing them. You are showing them the way.

qa.q: What will happen to you now?
a: I go back into the mist, to wait with the others. A golden hilt... and one eye. They are there. I can feel them.
When you come to Sovngarde, we will be waiting. Three old voices, ready to shout beside you one more time.
Thank you, Dragonborn. Until Sovngarde.

lore.title: The Echo Altars and their four trials
lore.lead: The same four trials in every city, each with the city's own places, one after another, all at night, the party sharing them. The last seal calls the city's Dragon Priest out at once; his fall frees the city.

items.s: Slay the risen in the altar's light
items.d: Alduin's mist bars the road to Sovngarde, and the dead of the city have nowhere to go. Put them down within the light of the city's Echo Altar and their souls rise through the mist at last. Lay a number of of the risen to rest in the altar's light.

items.s: Find the place the altar's voice names
items.d: At night a voice speaks from the Echo Altar of the city, and it speaks in riddles. Find the place it names, and hold it against the dead: slay a number of of the risen there.

items.s: Stand in the altar's light until it closes
items.d: When the Tongues first woke their altars, the light had to be held while Alduin's dead came for it. At night, step into the light of the Echo Altar of the city: it begins to draw in toward the stone, and every one of the risen in the city comes for you. Stay inside the ring until it closes on the stone. Step out and the light falters and slips back.

items.s: Shatter the Dragon Priest's three seals
items.d: The Dragon Priest who holds the altar of the city silent has bound it with three seals of dragon script, set at the city's great places and each kept by one of his chosen. Kill each guard and strike its seal. When the last one breaks, the priest comes out to meet you.

lore.title: The cities and their Dragon Priests
lore.lead: Ten cities, each with its altar, its trials' places and its Dragon Priest. Each priest drops his own relic to every player when he falls.

items.d: Hits shackle the dead in place. Heavy: chains yank the nearby dead together.
Hits blind the dead: they slow and hit weaker. Heavy: a fog where they wander lost.
Light: a gust that staggers the dead 8 m ahead. Heavy: a 12 m cone that knocks them down.
Hits freeze the dead until they die. Heavy: shatters every frozen one around you.
Hits chain lightning to 2 more of the dead. Heavy: lightning arcs to all around you.
Hits poison, spreading to the next of the dead. Heavy: every poisoned one bursts.
Hits heal you 1%. Heavy: a wail that weakens the dead around you.
Hits shatter armour. Heavy: a shockwave that staggers all around you.
Hits put the dead to sleep. Heavy: a nightmare fog that slows them.
Hits burst with magic. Heavy: a magicka shockwave that refills your magicka.

a: The mill wheel turns, and no red light falls over the barrow. Listen... it is a quiet valley again.
This was the first stone you woke. I will remember that.

qa.q: What was Riverwood like in your time?
a: When we raised this stone, there was no town here. Only the river, and a dragon's nest on the mountain above it.
The Gildergreen is quiet. The plains are only grass again.
Nahkriin's gate has one less keeper. The road to Sovngarde is a little clearer for it.

qa.q: What was Whiterun like in your time?
a: The dragon in Dragonsreach was not the first caged on that hill. The first was there in our time. We heard it screaming for a year.
The arch over the sea is quiet. The bards can sing of the dead again, instead of to them.
Solitude will tell this story for a hundred years. They will get it wrong. Let them.

qa.q: What was Solitude like in your time?
a: There were Tongues who lived on these cliffs, and taught their students to shout across the water. The sea still remembers the sound.
The candle still burns, and nothing comes to it but the living.
Windhelm has buried enough of its own. It can rest now.

qa.q: What was Windhelm like in your time?
a: Ysgramor's people built over the stone without knowing it was here. It has listened to every king of Windhelm since.
The stone city is still. Even the Reach's oldest dead have gone back to sleep.
Otar is gone. I will not mourn him. Neither did his cult.

qa.q: What was Markarth like in your time?
a: The deep elves had a stone of their own, under the cliff. Ours answered it once. Nothing answers from down there now.
The canal is only water again. The thieves can go back to stealing from the living.
Rahgot's followers died for him twice. Let them stay dead this time.

qa.q: What was Riften like in your time?
a: The lake here was a holy place to Mara before there was a city. We raised the stone where her pilgrims rested.
The rows are quiet. Falkreath can bury its dead and leave them buried.
Krosis grieved for a thousand years. I hope he has stopped.

qa.q: What was Falkreath like in your time?
a: Even in our time, people came here to bury their dead. Some places are made for grief.
The fog is only fog again. Morthal can sleep with its doors unbarred.
Hevnoraak's servants were right to seal him. You finished what they started.

qa.q: What was Morthal like in your time?
a: The marsh swallowed the first stone we raised here. This is the second. We were careful where we put it.
The harbour is frozen and still. Tonight, Dawnstar will sleep without dreaming.
The nightmares are over here. For once, the dreamers will wake rested.

qa.q: What was Dawnstar like in your time?
a: There was a shrine in the hills here to a god of dreams. We built the stone well away from it. We were right to.
The storm has passed. The bridge to the College is only a bridge again.
Morokei is gone, and the College will claim the credit. Let it.

qa.q: What was Winterhold like in your time?
a: This stone once stood in a great city. The sea took the city. The stone held on. So did the College.

lore.title: Your class and its wonder
lore.lead: Each class has its own place in the story and its own wonder, earned by a hidden quest that Felldir whispers.

a: The stone offers four ways to fight the dead. The Tongues walked all of them, once.
The Summoner, who calls the dead's own kind to fight them. The Destruction mage, who burns them where they stand.
The Alchemist, who bottles every element and pours it out. The Spellsword, steel in one hand and a spell in the other.
Choose at the stone. Choosing again later costs dearly, so choose well.
The stone will let you. It will cost you fifty thousand of the essence the dead leave behind.
Your kit stays your own. But your path's powers stay with the path.

qa.q: What do you see in me?
a: You call things to fight for you, and they come. The Tongues had a word for people like you. It was not a kind word.
But it was a useful one. The dead fear what does not fear them.
Fire. Frost. Storm. You do not ask the dead to sleep. You make them.
The Tongues had mages like you. The dragons learned to fear them... for a while.
You bottle what the rest of us fear. Fire in glass, frost in glass... even, one day, the curse itself.
The Tongues never trusted alchemists. They trusted their potions well enough.
Steel in one hand, a spell in the other. You fight the way the first Tongues fought, before they had the Voice.
You get closer to the dead than anyone should. They feel it.

qa.q: Teach me of the Summoner's craft.
a: Let your servants hold the line. You are the one who must not fall. Without you, they go back where they came from.
The more you call, the thinner you are spread. Be wise about it.

qa.q: Is there a wonder for my path?
a: There is. The Soulcaller's Staff. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
There is. The Wyrmspine Javelin. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
There is. The Mutagen Staff. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
There is. The Dragon Slayer. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
Listen... the ghost-cats that guarded the Tongues still prowl. Their souls are scattered. Gather them.
Follow them quietly at night, near a freed stone. They fear the hunter. They will come to a patient one.
A god's eye fell to Nirn, and the curse buried its light. The Eye of Magnus... its pieces are falling again.
When a star crosses the sky above you at night, strike it down. That is where the path begins.
Every element can be bottled. Brew the Elixir of Aetherius... and the Mutagen Staff will answer you.
One of the dead burns brighter than the rest. Break it with glass... and catch what falls.
A slayer once swore an oath and broke his blade on the World-Eater's scales. The pieces are scattered.
Take up his oath. Where the World-Eater first returned, a broken blade waits for a hand. Begin there.
The Soulcaller's Staff. Every soul it takes is one the dead will never get back.
At twenty souls the pride answers. They remember who freed them.
The Wyrmspine Javelin. Carved from a dragon's spine, and it remembers the sky.
Throw it hard. It wants to fly again.
The Mutagen Staff. Six vials of the world's elements, poured through one orb.
The Elixir of Aetherius was only ever a story. You made it true.
The Dragon Slayer. Every blow carries the spell in your other hand.
The slayer's oath is kept. He would have been glad of you.

qa.q: Did the Tongues fight like me?
a: One of us could call the wolves down from the mountain with a word. They followed her to the summit. None of them came back.
Our fire-callers burned the dragons' priests out of their towers. The dragons answered in kind. Fire was cheap in those days.
We had a healer who brewed in a skull, because it was the only bowl she had. She kept more of us alive than the Voice did.
Before the Voice, we had steel and a little magic, and we fought dragons with that. Most of us died. The ones who lived taught the rest.

qa.q: Teach me of the Destruction mage's craft.
a: Your power is in your magicka, and your magicka runs out. Never let the dead catch you empty.
Each element has its use. Fire for the crowd. Frost to slow them. Storm for whatever is still standing.

qa.q: Teach me of the Alchemist's craft.
a: Your flasks are your strength. Know which element the dead fear, and give them that one.
Never stand still to brew. The dead do not wait for anything to cool.

qa.q: Teach me of the Spellsword's craft.
a: Your blade carries your spell. Choose the spell before you choose the fight.
Get close, and stay close. A Spellsword at the edge of a fight is only half of one.
Each of you walks a path of your own. Together, you are what the Tongues were. Stay together.
If one of you falls, the rest of you lift them. The dead do not take prisoners.

lore.title: The hidden quests (Easter eggs)
lore.lead: The wonders still sleep. Free more cities, and they will stir. Each wonder's quest has five steps, whispered by Felldir one at a time; the reward waits in the great hall of High Hrothgar.

eggs.reward: The Greybeards call you to High Hrothgar: the Soulcaller's Staff waits in the great hall.
eggs.open: Listen... the ghost-cats that guarded the Tongues still prowl. Gather their scattered souls, and the Soulcaller's Staff will answer you.

steps.d: Calm the three spirit sabre cats roaming within 200 m of the altar at night - sneak up on each
steps.hint: Three spirit cats stalk the edges of this city by moonlight. They fear the hunter. Come to them quietly.

steps.d: The hunt: 30 of the dead slain by your summons at night, a spirit cat at your side
steps.hint: A pride must hunt. Let your servants kill thirty of the dead tonight, and keep the spirit at your side alive.

steps.d: Touch the four roaring stones in the order you heard them
steps.hint: Four stones remember the pride's roar. Listen to the order they call, then answer them.

steps.d: Hold the altar against the dead without striking a blow yourself - only your summons may kill
steps.hint: Stand at this altar while the dead come. Lift no blade. Let only what you call do the killing.

steps.d: Break the Bone-Caller's three soul-chains, then kill him
steps.hint: The Bone-Caller chains the Old King's soul. Break the chains, then break him.

whispers: Listen... the ghost-cats that guarded the Tongues still prowl. Gather their scattered souls, and the Soulcaller's Staff will answer you.
Three spirit cats stalk the edges of this city by moonlight. They fear the hunter. Come to them quietly.
Three souls pad behind you now.
A pride must hunt. Let your servants kill thirty of the dead tonight, and keep the spirit at your side alive.
The pride has tasted the hunt.
Four stones remember the pride's roar. Listen to the order they call, then answer them.
The roar is whole again.
Stand at this altar while the dead come. Lift no blade. Let only what you call do the killing.
The den is ready.
The Bone-Caller chains the Old King's soul. Break the chains, then break him.
The Old King runs free.
The pride is whole. The Greybeards are calling. The Soulcaller's Staff waits at High Hrothgar.

eggs.reward: The Greybeards call you to High Hrothgar: the Wyrmspine Javelin waits in the great hall.
eggs.open: A god's eye fell to Nirn, and the curse buried its light. Wake its fire, frost and storm, and the Wyrmspine Javelin is yours to claim.

steps.d: Open the ember, rime and storm seals, each with a spell of its element, within 20 seconds of the first
steps.hint: Three seals sleep near this altar: ember, rime and storm. Strike each with its own element, before the first goes dark again.

steps.d: Catch five falling pieces of the Eye at night within 60 seconds
steps.hint: Pieces of the Eye are falling tonight. Catch five before they burn out.

steps.d: Strike the four light-stones in order: fire, frost, storm, then sun
steps.hint: Four stones, four colours. Ember before frost, frost before storm, and storm before the sun. Strike them so.

steps.d: 40 of the dead slain with Destruction at night - at least 10 each by fire, frost and storm
steps.hint: Burn forty of the dead tonight. Fire, frost and storm... the Eye hungers for all three.

steps.d: Unmake the Great Anomaly - strike it only with an element it isn't wearing
steps.hint: The Great Anomaly wears every element in turn. Strike it with what it fears, never with what it wears.

whispers: A god's eye fell to Nirn, and the curse buried its light. Wake its fire, frost and storm, and the Wyrmspine Javelin is yours to claim.
Three seals sleep near this altar: ember, rime and storm. Strike each with its own element, before the first goes dark again.
The seals are open.
Pieces of the Eye are falling tonight. Catch five before they burn out.
The light is gathered.
Four stones, four colours. Ember before frost, frost before storm, and storm before the sun. Strike them so.
The prism shines.
Burn forty of the dead tonight. Fire, frost and storm... the Eye hungers for all three.
The Eye is kindled.
The Great Anomaly wears every element in turn. Strike it with what it fears, never with what it wears.
The Anomaly is unmade.
The Eye sees again. The Greybeards are calling. The Wyrmspine Javelin waits at High Hrothgar.

eggs.reward: The Greybeards call you to High Hrothgar: the Mutagen Staff waits in the great hall.
eggs.open: Every element can be bottled... even the curse. Brew the Elixir of Aetherius, and the Mutagen Staff will be yours.

steps.d: Kill the six element-wrapped dead at night, each with a flask of its own element, and take their essences
steps.hint: Six of the dead rise tonight, each wrapped in an element. Answer each with its own flask, and take what falls.

steps.d: Carry the essences to the altar before dawn

a: ...where the mill wheel turns beside the river, over the hill from where the dragon first broke the sky.
...beneath the hall built on a dragon's cage, where the golden tree grows.
...where the great arch spans the sea, and the bards keep their songs.
...in the oldest city of stone, where the snow never leaves the palace of kings.
...in the city the deep elves carved, where the cliffs bleed silver.
...where the canals run beneath a city of thieves and honey.
...among the graves in the pines, where the dead outnumber the living.
...in the marsh town, where the mist hides what walks.
...on the cold northern shore, where the dreamers cannot sleep.
...where the city fell into the sea, and the college stands alone.
A lone spirit walks the night. Follow it softly... and see where it leads.
When a star crosses the sky above you... strike it down.
One of the dead burns brighter than the rest. Break it with glass, and catch what falls.
Where the World-Eater first returned, a broken blade waits for a hand.
Two stones wake... so you can hear me. These altars were old before your Empire was born. They were raised while dragons still ruled the sky.
We raised them, the three of us... the first who learned the Voice and turned it on its masters. One fell at the summit. One I have not seen since. And I... I am still here.
Six stones are free... you may hear my name. I am Felldir the Old. I read the Scroll that cast Alduin out of time, and I wait for you behind his mist. The wonders stir... watch the night.

alchemist.why: The Alchemist turns the dead into fuel: brands, catalysts and transmutation.
moves: A wide sweep that cuts every one of the dead in front of you and sets them smouldering in shadowfire; the burn stacks with each swing.
Each hit marks the dead with a violet catalyst; a marked one that dies bursts, burning the ones beside it.
Hits leave a corroding brand that eats armour and spreads to the next of the dead it touches.
The blade driven into the ground: geysers of shadowfire burst up in a ring round you (your kit pick).
A full spinning reap that pulls the dead within 5 m in toward you and cuts them all.
The slam turns the dead within 4 m to burning ash statues that shatter when struck.
Every 10th kill transmutes: the next of the dead you kill bursts into Cursed Essence and shadowfire.
Kills sometimes drop a cracked flask that bursts in shadowfire a second later.
Every 4th hit, a violet ghost of the scythe slashes beside you on its own.

summoner.why: The Summoner fights beside what it calls: marks for its servants, light from the sky, spirits on command.
moves: Each strike flares with sunlight that sears the dead and blinds them for a moment.
Each strike sends a small spirit off the staff that seeks out another of the dead.
Each strike marks the dead: your summons go for the marked first, and hit them harder.
Both heads driven down: a pillar of sunlight pours onto the spot (your kit pick).
The slam calls two spectral wolves out of the light to hunt for 8 s.
A circle of runes where your summons heal and the dead burn.
Every 15 kills, your summons blaze with light: half again as strong for 10 s.
Every 20 kills, a spectral Nord warrior rises from the light and fights beside you for 12 s.
Three orbs of light circle you and strike the dead that come close.

destruction.why: The Battle-mage is the caster: a tap fires, a hold channels, and power builds the longer you keep it up.
moves: Tap: the bolt (0.5 s between shots)
A tap fires a glintstone bolt that bends a little toward the nearest of the dead.
A tap fires three smaller bolts in a fan.
A tap fires a narrow ray that passes through the first of the dead into the next.
Hold: a beam of raw magicka that grows wider and hotter the longer you hold it.
Hold: a beam that forks to two more of the dead near the one it holds.
Hold: a beam that burns a line through the dead; what it kills bursts in magicka.
Every 25th bolt, twelve great bolts rain down in front of you.
Beam kills leave a rune that bursts a second later.
Beam kills refill your magicka, and your next tap fires three bolts.

spellsword.why: The Spellsword fuses blade and spell: the other hand's element rides every move.
moves: Each thrust carries the spell in your other hand: fire burns, frost slows, shock arcs to one more.
Block a blow just in time and the counter-thrust strikes three times as hard in a burst of your element.
Every 3rd thrust is a quick double thrust.
A pillar of your element pours down on the one you strike (your kit pick).
You dash 6 m through the dead, leaving a trail of your element.
A long lance of your element pierces everything in a line.
Each spell cast with your other hand charges the blade: your next heavy is twice as strong.
Kills leave a patch of your element on the ground that burns, freezes or shocks the dead that cross it.
Go 5 s without being hit and your next thrust is a sure critical.

sections: The game

Skyrim played as Black Ops 3 Zombies: nights of the dead in each of Skyrim's 10 Dragon Priest cities (Riverwood, Whiterun, Solitude, Windhelm, Markarth, Riften, Falkreath, Morthal, Dawnstar, Winterhold), rounds that climb, Cursed Essence earned on every kill.
The dead come down red beams of light from the sky. No XP from them; no casters, archers or shouting enemies at night (Dragon Priests and dragons keep their powers).

The dead (Nov 26, your keep/remove marks): Mihail's zombies (walkers, headless, dread, deranged runners), our six Thriceborn, Rag Draugr and Restless Rag Draugr, Rotten and Bloody Skeletons, the Feral Death Hound, the Hulking Draugr, Ash Spawn and Immolators, the Frost Brute, the Hunger, the Ogrim and the Winged Twilight. Bosses: Grimmvar (a Vile dragon, every 10th night), the Hunting Ground King (from 10), Gehenoth (from 15), Grahzah (a level-4 Necro dragon, from 20). Mini-bosses: the Giant Brute Berserker, Minotaur Lord, Ogrim Lord and a Plague Dragon. 99 others taken out.

Dragons are half size and fly as Skyrim flies them; a dragon boss's breath and the dead it calls land on the ground near you. The three word-dragons: Sanguine (flesh), Aether (time), Otherworld (undoing); the Echo of Alduin a level-7 Dark dragon.

Bosses: night 5 one of your kept mini-bosses at random (Giant Brute, Minotaur Lord, Ogrim Lord, Plague Dragon), the Hunting Ground King from 10, Gehenoth from 15, Grahzah from 20. No noise hunter (off since Nov 17).

Movement (your BO3 movement): the sprint winds up (180 ms) to 440 and widens the view 7 degrees; the slide (sprint + crouch) tilts the view 3 degrees and its speed carries into a jump; light swings 1.2x.

The ability ladder: the class weapons' Tier I light ability, Tier II heavy, Tier III ultimate from a 25-kill meter (Aetherial Host, Starfall, Soul Harvest, Spell Lance); each Ascend +15% damage, +10% size.

On screen: the night counter a plain number top left with the quests under it; the essence bottom left; the held weapon's card bottom right; the ultimate's meter above the perks; no banners or hints; a 10 s countdown before a night only.

Loading screens: 123 of the Load Screen Compendium's that fit the Curse, at random; our own Curse of Alduin screen when a saved game loads from the main menu. Sounds: every weapon its own draw, swing, heavy and hit; the abilities on their picked or recommended sounds; all at 20%.

Deaths: a kill by shadow, spirit or arcane tears the soul out (a white beam, Alduin's soul sound); heavies throw the body at half strength; fire kills burn to a pile of ash; the rest through FEC, as you chose.
Free every city at its Echo Altar; the questline ends right before Skyrim's own Alduin fight. The last three dragons and the Echo of Alduin are the hardest fights.
Solo first; co-op for 1 to 4 players (Skyrim Together, optional). Releasing free on Nexus.
Special nights: The Pack, Daedric Incursion, Armored Champions, Blood Fog.
After night 10: kill essence tapers, and Tablet, upgrade and Armory prices rise 3% a night (brews stay fixed).
Hit feel: no hit pause and no shake (Nov 26). Bodies fly half as far (Alduin's Bane as before).
New character
One loading screen from NEW to the character creator (sliders only, by body area); our own launch screen (the Alduin painting) and menu music.
At Riverwood you choose your Helgen companion (Ralof or Hadvar) and Survival Mode on or off. No starting weapons. Skyrim's own underwear on both bodies (3BA, HIMBO).
The class is chosen later, at the Echo Altar (changing it costs 50,000 Cursed Essence; one shared inventory).
Each city: the Echo Altar

Four trials, in order, at night, shared by the party: Lay the Restless to Rest (souls fly to the stone as white fireballs, the ring of light fills smoothly), The Stone's Whisper (Felldir's Whisper once six are free), Hold the Light, Break the Priest's Seals.
The last seal calls the city's Dragon Priest at once; his fall frees the city and drops his relic to every player.
Felldir the Old speaks from each freed altar's centre stone (his own ElevenLabs voice, a short stone echo, centred subtitles). Talk: four topics, 244 lines and 67 whispers, opening as the story goes.
The altar menu: choose your class, Your Kit (claim your weapon, armour set and spells), the Armory, the Tablet of Mysteries, brews.
The four classes
Summoner: the Radiant Quarterstaff (Steel, Ebony, Daedric, Dragonbone by tier), conjurations of our own; wonder: the Soulcaller's Staff; Necromancer robes.
Battle-mage (Destruction): the Carian Wand (Steel, Stalhrim, Glass, Daedric by tier), Destruction spells; wonder: the Wyrmspine Javelin (tap jabs, hold throws); Arch-Mage's robes.
Alchemist: the Shadowflame Scythe (Forsworn, Falmer, Dwarven, Dragon Priest by tier; sheathe it for your flasks), six flasks; wonder: the Mutagen Staff; Morag Tong set.
Spellsword: the Spellbound Rapier (Steel, Ebony, Daedric, Dragonbone by tier; its look follows the spell in your other hand), touch spells; wonder: the Dragon Slayer; Ahzidal's set.

Every item climbs Base, Tier I, II, III and Ascended. Ascended adds damage only; it keeps Tier III's model. Class weapons wear their look from Tier I. Class sets: hoods only, a class-colour aura that grows; Tier III sets breathe and trail wisps.
